question.problem: Find the equation of the tangent hyperplane to the hypersurface $w=2x{y}^{2}+y{z}^{2}-3{x}^{2}z$ at the point $(2,-2,1,2).$
question.worked_solution:
The Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the hypersurface $w=f(x,y,z)$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0},{w}_{0})$ on the hypersurface can be written as

$$
w-{w}_{0}=(x-{x}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂x}({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})+(y-{y}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂y}({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})+(z-{z}_{0})\frac{∂f}{∂z}({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0}).
$$

First, we find the partial derivatives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2x{y}^{2}+y{z}^{2}-3{x}^{2}z)=2{y}^{2}-6xz \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2x{y}^{2}+y{z}^{2}-3{x}^{2}z)=4xy+{z}^{2} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(2x{y}^{2}+y{z}^{2}-3{x}^{2}z)=2yz-3{x}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate the partial derivatives at $(x,y,z)=(2,-2,1):$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x}(2,-2,1) & =2(-2)^{2}-6(2)(1)=-4 \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y}(2,-2,1) & =4(2)(-2)+(1)^{2}=-15 \\ \frac{∂f}{∂z}(2,-2,1) & =2(-2)(1)-3(2)^{2}=-16\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write down the equation of the tangent hyperplane:

$$
\begin{aligned}w-2 & =(x-2)\frac{∂f}{∂x}(2,-2,1)+(y+2)\frac{∂f}{∂y}(2,-2,1)+(z-1)\frac{∂f}{∂z}(2,-2,1) \\ w-2 & =-4(x-2)-15(y+2)-16(z-1) \\ w-2 & =-4x+8-15y-30-16z+16 \\ 4x+15y+16z+w+4 & =0\end{aligned}
$$
